chain.label: Captain leaves fuel tank shutoff valve open during crossfeed
chain.trigger: the captain intentionally kept the valve open because he thought that Convair fuel tank shutoff valves tended to fail after being shut off

chain.label: Inadequate preflight weight-and-balance planning
chain.trigger: he did not leave a copy of the load manifest at MEM...because he had to manually calculate the airplane's weight and balance, and the calculations were not completed before takeoff

chain.label: Captain preoccupied, fails to monitor crossfeed/gauges, starts in-range checklist late
chain.trigger: he was 'preoccupied' with and 'stressed' about calculating the airplane's weight and balance

caused_by.evidence: Because the captain used the incorrect fuel burn moment value, the calculations were not computing correctly, and the captain became preoccupied with trying to identify the mistake

chain.label: Captain ignores first officer's repeated reports of abnormal control forces
chain.trigger: The captain did not respond to the first officer's first five comments regarding the airplane's unusual handling characteristics

caused_by.evidence: he was preoccupied with the weight and balance calculations during critical portions of the flight and, as a result, he did not monitor the fuel crossfeed operations

chain.label: Fuel transfers from left tank into right tank through open valve during crossfeed
chain.trigger: all of the fuel from the left fuel tank not used by the engines could transfer into the right fuel tank in a relatively short period of time

caused_by.evidence: wreckage examinations confirmed that both the left and right fuel tank shutoff valves were open at impact
the crew missed several opportunities to identify the ongoing fuel crossfeed operations and determine that the airplane's fuel was imbalanced

chain.label: Left fuel tank exhausted of fuel
chain.trigger: the fuel in the left fuel tank, which was providing fuel to both engines, was exhausted

caused_by.evidence: all of the fuel from the airplane's left tank that was not used by the engines transferred into the right tank

chain.label: Dual-engine flameout on short final
chain.trigger: we're losing power...we've lost both of them

caused_by.evidence: when the left fuel tank was exhausted of fuel, the left fuel boost pump most likely continued to operate, which allowed air to enter the fuel system...resulting in a dual-engine flameout

chain.label: Airplane strikes trees and terrain short of runway
chain.trigger: The wreckage was located about 1.2 miles short of runway 36R

caused_by.evidence: the pilots most likely would not have had sufficient time or altitude to restart the engines because they lost power during short final approach

chain.label: First officer killed, captain minorly injured
chain.trigger: the first officer was killed, and the captain received minor injuries

caused_by.evidence: The airplane was destroyed by impact forces
